body:
From protest movements to organised social service

Tribal reform in modern India was not confined to religious preaching or political agitation. Voluntary organisations also attempted to improve access to schooling, social services and opportunities for communities facing poverty and exploitation.

One important Gujarat example is the Bhil Seva Mandal, associated with Amritlal Vithaldas Thakkar, popularly known as Thakkar Bapa.

Foundation and work in Dahod

The Bhil Seva Mandal was established in Dahod, in eastern Gujarat, to work for the welfare of Bhil and other Adivasi communities. The institution's own historical account dates its establishment to 1923.

Its beginnings were connected with efforts to respond to poverty, famine-related hardship, lack of education and social exploitation. Thakkar Bapa supported practical welfare work and placed particular importance on education.

The Mandal developed ashram schools and other educational activities. An ashram school is a residential school where children study and live, particularly useful where children face difficulties accessing ordinary schools because of distance or social disadvantage.

Early educational work associated with the Mandal included places such as Mirakhedi, Jeswada and Jhalod in the Dahod region. These initiatives sought to make schooling accessible to children who had previously had limited opportunities to study.

How welfare organisations differed from religious movements

The work of the Bhil Seva Mandal should be distinguished from the movements led by Birsa Munda, Jatra Oraon and Govind Guru. Those movements developed around community leaders and programmes combining religious reform with resistance to exploitation. The Bhil Seva Mandal was a voluntary social-service organisation that emphasised education and community welfare.

Both approaches responded to disadvantages faced by Adivasi communities, but their primary methods were different. A movement might mobilise followers through preaching, moral rules or collective protest; a welfare organisation could provide schools, relief and ongoing educational support.

One-glance comparison of the major movements

For prelims, the most useful way to distinguish these developments is to associate each one with its leader or institution, community, region and principal objective. The following summary brings together the essential relationships:

Prelims focus

  • Thakkar Bapa: Amritlal Vithaldas Thakkar.
  • Bhil Seva Mandal: voluntary tribal welfare and educational organisation centred in Dahod.
  • 1923: establishment year given in the Mandal's own institutional history.
  • Mirakhedi, Jeswada and Jhalod: places associated with early educational work in the Dahod region.
  • Trap: Bhil Seva Mandal was an educational and welfare institution, not the organisation that led the Mangarh gathering of 1913.

[Sources: Bhil Seva Mandal, Dahod, official institutional website, sections 'History' and 'Donation' (consulted 20 November 2026); Bhil Seva Mandal, 103rd Annual Report, reporting year ending 31 March 2025, institutional history section; Press Information Bureau, 'Mangarh Dham ki Gaurav Gatha', 1 November 2022, background on Govind Guru and Mangarh.]

title: Bhil Seva Mandal and the Role of Education in Tribal Upliftment
